title: Yara and the Songbook
premise: Mara Pemberton has rebuilt her life around her daughter, her bookshop, and a carefully guarded heart after her ex abandoned them — but when her sister's wedding forces her to bring a date, she impulsively asks Theo Marsh, the quiet musician who repairs instruments next door, to play the part. What begins as a transactional arrangement deepens through shared Sundays, a rediscovered songbook of Theo's late mother's compositions, and Mara's slow reckoning with the shame she carries about her own past choices. When Theo's record-label opportunity pulls him to Nashville and Mara's ex resurfaces threatening custody, both must decide whether love is something they survive or something they choose. In the end, Theo turns down the tour, Mara forgives the woman in the mirror, and they open the bookshop's back room as a small music school — a found family built on second chances finally taken.
about_author: T. M. Halloran is the pen name of a former small-town bookseller who now writes warm, music-soaked romance from a converted attic studio. Their novels explore the quiet courage of ordinary people choosing love after loss.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara opens the wedding invitation and feels the old dread — her family's pity dressed as celebration. Her daughter Lily asks innocently if she'll be alone again. Emotional beat: loneliness sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: The Man Next Door
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Theo Marsh tunes a piano in his repair shop while Mara restocks next door; their first real conversation happens over a broken violin Lily drags in. Emotional beat: unexpected warmth, quickly guarded against.

chapters.title: A Reckless Offer
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Cornered by her mother's phone call, Mara blurts to Theo that she needs a date for the reunion weekend. He surprises her by saying yes — for a price she assumes is money. Emotional beat: reckless hope.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo negotiates: not cash, but her help cataloguing his mother's old songbook, which he can't bring himself to open. Emotional beat: grief disguised as a business deal.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. They draft a list of rules over coffee — no real feelings, no past questions. Lily immediately likes Theo, which unsettles Mara more than she admits. Emotional beat: comedy over cracks.

chapters.title: The Drive Up
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The three-hour drive to her hometown; small talk turns dangerous when Theo asks about Lily's father and Mara shuts down. Emotional beat: the first hairline fracture.

chapters.title: Arrivals
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The family reunion opens with her sister Priya's engagement party; Mara performs happiness while relatives whisper. Theo plays along flawlessly. Emotional beat: performance as armor.

chapters.title: By Dessert
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Under the table, Theo's hand steadies hers during her aunt's cruel toast; afterward they laugh in the kitchen and the fake date feels dangerously real. Emotional beat: the mask slipping.

chapters.title: The Songbook
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Back home, Theo shows Mara his mother's handwritten songbook for the first time; she reads a lyric aloud and he has to leave the room. Emotional beat: grief surfacing.

chapters.title: What the Neighbors Saw
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Town gossip declares them a couple; Mara corrects everyone too quickly and regrets it when Theo's face falls. Emotional beat: unintended cruelty.

chapters.title: Rain Check
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A storm traps them in the bookshop after hours; Theo almost tells her about the night his mother died, but stops. Emotional beat: proximity without honesty.

chapters.title: Lily's Recital
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Lily's school recital; Theo quietly fixes a cracked cello for the music teacher and Mara watches him with the children and aches. Emotional beat: want acknowledged, then denied.

chapters.title: The Ex Returns
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Lily's father, Daniel, appears at the bookshop claiming he wants to be a father now — and drops the word 'custody.' Emotional beat: fear as a physical blow.

chapters.title: Fake Boyfriend, Real Ally
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo offers to be her stability on paper; Mara accepts, hating that the arrangement now has a second, darker use. Emotional beat: gratitude tangled with guilt.

chapters.title: Chapter and Verse
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara and Theo catalog the songbook together; she finds a dedication to a name no one in his family mentions. Emotional beat: curiosity as intimacy.

chapters.title: Priya's Warning
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Sister-to-sister, Priya warns Mara not to use Theo as a shield and to stop punishing herself for Daniel's leaving. Emotional beat: truth that stings because it's kind.

chapters.title: The Lawyer's Letter
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Daniel's lawyer requests a home study; Mara spirals, cleaning, cataloging, controlling everything except her fear. Emotional beat: the price of survival made visible.

chapters.title: Duet
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo teaches Lily a simple song from the songbook; Mara hears her daughter laughing through the wall and realizes the found family already exists. Emotional beat: terror of wanting it.

chapters.title: The First Kiss
chapters.summary: Dual POV. After the home study visit goes well, relief tips into a kiss in the bookshop doorway — immediately followed by both of them retreating to the rules. Emotional beat: joy followed by panic.

chapters.title: Rules, Broken
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara tries to reinstate the rules; Theo refuses to pretend, and they fight about who is protecting whom. Emotional beat: honest anger as progress.

chapters.title: Nashville Calling
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A label scout hears Theo's demo of his mother's song and offers a development deal in Nashville — three months, maybe forever. Emotional beat: dream and dilemma arriving together.

chapters.title: The Secret Name
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara discovers the dedication name belongs to Theo's estranged brother, who blames Theo for their mother's death. Emotional beat: understanding the locked room at last.

chapters.title: Brothers
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo visits his brother; the confrontation reveals he was driving the night of the accident. Emotional beat: guilt's long sentence.

chapters.title: Confession
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo tells Mara everything; she holds him, but he sees her flinch at the word 'accident' and misreads it. Emotional beat: vulnerability met with her own unspoken wound.

chapters.title: Mara's Mirror
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Alone, Mara confronts the night she chose not to chase Daniel — the shame that she 'let' her family fracture. Emotional beat: the enemy in the mirror named.

chapters.title: Home Study, Take Two
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The caseworker visits; Theo is there, and the inspector notes the household looks 'settled' — Mara realizes she's using him and hates it. Emotional beat: guilt compounding.

chapters.title: The Offer She Can't Refuse
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Daniel offers to drop custody if Mara signs away primary residency to her parents' town — control disguised as compromise. Emotional beat: survival's ugly arithmetic.

chapters.title: Crossroads
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo must sign the Nashville contract by Friday; he asks Mara, obliquely, to give him a reason to stay. She can't yet. Emotional beat: love asking for courage she doesn't have.

chapters.title: Priya's Wedding
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. At the wedding, Mara watches Theo dance with Lily and finally admits to herself she loves him — out loud, to Priya, in the coat room. Emotional beat: admission before action.

chapters.title: Friday Night
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Theo leaves the contract unsigned on his table and comes to the bookshop; Mara, mid-crisis over Daniel's ultimatum, pushes him away 'for his own good.' Emotional beat: self-sabotage as sacrifice.

chapters.title: Gone
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Theo signs and leaves for Nashville; the bookshop is silent except for Lily practicing his song alone. Emotional beat: the cost of protection.

chapters.title: The Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Weeks pass; Daniel's case advances, and Mara realizes the home study valued what she and Theo built, not what she can prove alone. Emotional beat: reckoning.

chapters.title: The Letter in the Songbook
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Cataloging the last pages, Mara finds Theo's mother's letter to her sons: 'the accident was not a verdict.' Emotional beat: absolution arriving by mail, years late.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. In court, Mara speaks plainly about her failures and her choices; Daniel's case collapses when his motives are exposed. Emotional beat: survival redefined as honesty.

chapters.title: Nashville, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. In Nashville, Theo can't record the song; his producer tells him to go home and live the lyric first. Emotional beat: art refusing to lie.

chapters.title: The Grand Gesture, Undone
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo returns, but Mara, stung and proud, tells him she won't be anyone's consolation prize. Emotional beat: the lowest point — love offered, refused.

chapters.title: Forgiving the Mirror
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. With Priya and Lily beside her, Mara finally forgives herself — writes a letter to the woman she was at twenty-four and burns it in the shop's back room. Emotional beat: the true climax, internal.

chapters.title: The Songbook, Finished
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo performs his mother's finished song at the bookshop's open mic, publicly forgiving himself; Mara is in the front row. Emotional beat: two absolutions meeting.

chapters.title: Second Chances, Better Timing
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Theo declines the tour permanently; Mara asks him to stay — not as a fake date, not as a shield, but as himself. He says yes. Emotional beat: choosing, not falling.

chapters.title: The Back Room
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, epilogue. One year later: the bookshop's back room is a music school, Lily teaches beginners, and the songbook sits open on a stand by the door. Emotional beat: found family, home at last.
